Written by hand.
A module that generates part of its own API. The zip carries the directives
and the generator, and not the file the generator writes.

The generator also writes over kept.go, which the zip DOES carry. The zip's
bytes win: what the module's authors published is the module.

-- .mod --
module example.com/generated

go 1.16
-- .info --
{"Version": "v1.0.0"}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/generated

go 1.16
-- gen/main.go --
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	out := flag.String("out", "", "file to write")
	over := flag.String("over", "", "file the module already ships, written anyway")
	flag.Parse()
	body := "package lang\n\nfunc Name() string { return \"generated\" }\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(*out, []byte(body), 0o666); err != nil {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if *over == "" {
		return
	}
	stale := "package lang\n\n// the generator wrote this\nconst Kept = \"the generator wrote this\"\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(*over, []byte(stale), 0o666); err != nil {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
-- lang/lang.go --
//go:generate go run example.com/generated/gen -out lang.gen.go -over kept.go

// Package lang declares nothing itself: Name is the generator's to write.
package lang
-- lang/kept.go --
package lang

// the module published this
const Kept = "the module published this"
